about: Every C++ engine test has a Rust counterpart of the same name (P3B_PLAN.md section 2.1, tools/ci/test_parity.py). Tests not listed here are mirrored in full: the Rust test counts the same expectations and feeds the engine the same frames. Listed tests say what differs and why.

tests.name: json & settings
tests.why: The JSON half is mirrored on vigil-formats. The other five expectations test the C++ settings registry (Setting::set step snapping and clamping, Settings::save/load), which is host code (core/settings) and stays in C++.

tests.name: presets keep defaults
tests.why: Applies the Balanced preset through a stand-in of the C++ registry (registerEngineSettings, Setting::set snapping, isDefault) so the claim - Balanced equals the declared defaults after the registry's snapping - is checked against the Rust declaration.

tests.name: config schema
tests.why: The expectation 'engine defaults equal the registry's defaults' goes through a stand-in of registerEngineSettings + configFromSettings; the declaration and default-configuration fixtures are compared byte for byte as in C++.

tests.name: config sync between frames
tests.why: The C++ registry and SettingsSync are replaced by a stand-in with the same rules (Setting::set, revision, sync only on change); every expectation about the engine's side (setConfig, monitoringEnabled, presets, refused and adopted snapshots) is checked against the Rust engine.

tests.name: config engines share nothing
tests.why: Mirrored except 'running engines never touches the settings registry': the C++ expectation guards the global registry; the Rust crate has no registry an engine could touch.

tests.name: settings keep unknown keys
tests.why: Tests only the C++ settings registry's file handling (core/settings). No Rust counterpart until the core layer is ported (RUST_PLAN.md section 4).
